curriculum.name: Particle model of solids, liquids and gases

questions.question: Which description best matches particles in a solid?
options: They vibrate around fixed positions
They move freely throughout the container
They do not move at all
They are widely spaced and move in all directions
questions.feedback: Particles in a solid vibrate around fixed positions.

curriculum.name: Particle model of solids, liquids and gases

questions.question: Why does liquid water take the shape of its container?
options: Its particles can move past one another
Its particles change shape
Its particles are fixed in place
Its particles spread out to fill all available space
questions.answer: Its particles can move past one another
questions.feedback: Liquid particles stay close together and can move past one another.

curriculum.name: Particle model of solids, liquids and gases

questions.question: Why is air easier to compress than liquid water?
options: Air particles have much more space between them
Air particles shrink when squeezed
Air particles stop moving under pressure
Water particles are larger than air particles
questions.answer: Air particles have much more space between them
questions.feedback: Compressing a gas reduces the spaces between its particles.

questions.question: What happens to the average speed of water particles as the liquid warms?
options: It increases
It decreases
It stays the same
It drops to zero
questions.feedback: As the temperature rises, the particles move faster on average.

questions.question: Water droplets form on the outside of a cold glass. Where did the water come from?
options: Water vapour in the surrounding air condensed
Liquid water passed through the glass
The glass produced water as it cooled
Water in the air froze directly onto the glass
questions.answer: Water vapour in the surrounding air condensed
questions.feedback: Water vapour cools near the glass and condenses into liquid droplets.

questions.question: Ice melts in a sealed container. What happens to the total mass of water inside?
options: It stays the same
It increases as the ice melts
It decreases as the ice melts
It depends on the shape of the container
questions.feedback: Melting changes the arrangement of the particles. The same water particles remain inside the sealed container.
